messages:
incident-bot: Pager duty alert -> PU-RESV-DQ-3: Dedicated-resv-pool 'east-us-2' high queue depth for reserved tenants. Severity: P2. Paging @oncall.

alice.l: saw the alert, joining. queue_length=~420, avg_wait=31s, gpu_util=98% across pool. Not seeing immediate VM OOM.

ben.sre: I'm on it. Checking autoscaler logs now. Last scale event failed with rate limit and scale cap.

carla.eng: linking autoscaler logs and router metrics: https://internal.redwood/metrics/173/queue?range=15m (redacted)

carla.eng: autoscaler stderr snippet:
```
ERROR: autoscale-controller: request to scale up rejected - reached tenant_reserved_limit (max_instances=24)
WARN: backoff applied for group=dedi-east-us-2, reason=no_capacity
```

ben.sre: that matches what I'm seeing. pool max_instances hit. There are several long-lived sessions from a single enterprise tenant (VelvetPay) pinned to reserved slots + a bunch of burst sessions from other tenants. Possible noisy neighbor.

erica.cust: VelvetPay support here — customers are reporting timeouts and 503s inside their app at ~10:27 UTC. They're calling support. We should assess impact ASAP and communicate.

dave.support: current inbound support tickets: 12 for VelvetPay, 3 for other enterprise tenants. SLA risk flagged.

fiona.ops: quick mitigation suggestions: 1) drain best-effort (burst) sessions, 2) evict >24h idle sessions, 3) bump reserved burst capacity if possible, 4) route VelvetPay to hosted fallback pool (if allowed). Which one do we do first?

alice.l: start with draining best-effort and evicting idle sessions. I'll run the drain script on pool 'dedi-east-us-2' for best-effort label. Need approval to evict idle >24h. @ben.sre?

ben.sre: approved. Running: `./scripts/drain_pool --pool dedi-east-us-2 --labels best-effort --grace 30`

ben.sre: drain kicked off. Expect ~90 sessions to be terminated over next 60s. Updating autoscaler triggers to ignore transient drop.

incident-bot: Action logged: ben.sre invoked drain_pool (run_id=rn-20260315-01).

carla.eng: also temporarily lowering the per-tenant session cap for VelvetPay to free slots: `configctl set tenant.velvetpay.max_slots 12 -> 8` (will take effect in 10s). This is an emergency throttle, rollback after capacity stabilizes.

alice.l: throttle applied. VelvetPay current sessions 14 -> will scale down to 8 as older sessions close. Monitor for errors.

ben.sre: drain completed. Evicted 94 best-effort sessions. Idle eviction removed 17 sessions >24h. pool gpu_util now 86%, queue_length ~120.

fiona.ops: good. Still above normal. Why didn't autoscaler open more instances? We hit tenant_reserved_limit (24) - that is per-tenant or per-pool?

carla.eng: it's per-pool hard cap tied to our ops quota for that AZ. We can request burst capacity but approval takes >30m. For immediate relief we can offload some VelvetPay traffic to the multi-tenant hosted fallback pool (policy allows for emergency fallback for enterprise with consent).

erica.cust: VelvetPay asks to avoid routing to shared pool unless necessary. They prefer we free their reserved slots first. Can we prioritize their leader sessions?

alice.l: suggestion: resume dedicated session preemption ordering: mark oldest non-critical sessions as preemptible and evict them first. We'll avoid killing active in-flight inference (requests with recent tokens). We'll run a selective eviction script.

ben.sre: running selective-evict: `selective-evict --pool dedi-east-us-2 --criteria "tenant!=velvetpay && idle>5m && not in-flight" --max 60`

ben.sre: selective-evict removed 58 sessions. pool gpu_util now 74%, queue_length 58, avg_wait 12s.

incident-bot: Update: incident status -> mitigation in progress. Responsible: ben.sre, alice.l, carla.eng.

dave.support: sending a customer update to VelvetPay: "We observed a surge in queueing due to cross-tenant activity; we've applied emergency throttling and selective evictions while we continue to stabilize. Expect improved latency within next 10-15 minutes. We're available on the bridge."

erica.cust: VelvetPay acknowledged, asked for a short post-incident note and root-cause details.

carla.eng: root cause hypothesis: a combination of a VelvetPay long-lived pinned session pattern + several burst jobs from other tenants pushing pool to the configured hard cap. Autoscaler couldn't scale due to pool-level quota cap. Also an autoscaler race where multiple scale attempts were rate-limited.

alice.l: next actions: 1) open ops ticket to request temporary increase of dedi-east-us-2 pool quota by +4 GPUs; 2) implement more aggressive session preemption policy for reserved pools; 3) add alert for per-tenant long-lived sessions > 8h. I'll own 2 and 3. ben owns 1.

ben.sre: created ticket OPS-12984 to request burst +4 GPUs (submitted). Contacted infra-aws team for expedited approval. ETA unknown.

fiona.ops: also rolling a short-term autoscaler tweak to relax rate-limits so it can retry faster in emergency windows. Patch applied to canary: `autoscaler.retry.backoff=5s` for emergency path. Will watch canary for 5m.

carla.eng: telemetry note: saved a snapshot of all KV caches and session metadata for investigation.

ben.sre: queue and latency trending down. At 15:40 UTC queue_length=18, avg_wait=3s, gpu_util 63%. VelvetPay reported improved performance at 15:42 UTC.

dave.support: closing customer bridge in 20m if stable. We'll follow up with postmortem and impact spreadsheet.

alice.l: good runbook followups: reduce per-pool hard cap dependency on single AZ, implement cross-pool emergency routing, and validate tenant slot accounting for long-lived sessions.

incident-bot: Incident update: mitigation successful, SLOs restored. Please file postmortem within 72 hours and add "VelvetPay reserved slot policy" to agenda.

fiona.ops: noted. I'll schedule a quick sync with infra (ops + eng + cust) tomorrow 09:00 UTC.

carla.eng: final logs attached to the incident ticket OPS-12984 (internal). Marking thread resolved in 30m unless new regressions show up. :white_check_mark:

ben.sre: +1. Great teamwork.
